title: Eliminate capacitor-hole etching: self-ordered anodic alumina pores become storage nodes
idea: Eliminate the HAR plasma etch, which needs helium backside cooling and argon-diluted plasmas: CVD aluminum from dimethylaluminum hydride (not argon sputtering), then anodize it in oxalic acid, guided by nanoimprinted dimples aligned to the transistor grid, to grow straight 20-30 nm pores at AR 100+. ALD with N2 purge and electroless Ru turn each pore into one capacitor.
why: Attacks fact 1 (AR 115 becomes cheap because pore depth is just anodizing time) and fact 4 (removes the costliest etch tool) using abundant materials; risk is pore registration to transistors at 30 nm pitch.

title: Anodized-aluminum capacitor forest: self-ordered 1000:1 pores without etching
idea: Copy architectural aluminum anodizing. Sputter 1 um of Al over the transistor array, imprint dimples aligned to the storage contacts, and anodize at ~10 V in sulfuric acid so pores self-order at ~25 nm pitch, one per dimple. ALD then lines each pore with TiN/TiO2-Al2O3/TiN.
why: Facts 4 and 1: a wet electrochemical bath with near-zero tool cost replaces the most expensive high-AR capacitor etch. AR >100 becomes trivial, giving >10 fF even at k~30.

title: Element passport: incentives only for cells built from domestic elements
idea: Box constraint as policy: CHIPS and DPA Title III funds and a federal purchasing preference go only to storage-element stacks whose every element (e.g., Si, Al, B, N, O, Hf, Zr, Mo, Cu, Zn, Fe, Ti, Pt/Pd, V, Te) has U.S. primary production, with matched loans for domestic high-purity Hf/Zr/Mo ALD-precursor plants. Each cell design files a bill of elements traced to a U.S. mine or refinery.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and U.S. manufacturability: steers R&D toward chokepoint-free stacks before fabs lock in W, Ru, Sc or Ga.

title: MiG-25 vacuum-tube engineer: floating island in sealed nano-vacuum
idea: A Soviet engineer under embargo trusts vacuum electronics because they shrug off radiation. The storage node is a metal nano-island suspended in a sealed 20 nm vacuum cavity with no dielectric and therefore no leakage path. Field emission from a sharp tip writes it, and the island's charge is read by how it modulates a neighbouring field-emission current.
why: Leakage-free storage removes refresh (fact 3) and the need for a high-k, high-AR capacitor (fact 1); a vacuum gap has no trap-assisted tunneling or dielectric wear, so endurance is effectively unlimited.

title: Vertical CCD pillars: bits climb a 100-gate stack instead of being addressed
idea: Reverse addressing: rather than moving the sense amp to the bit, clock charge packets up and down a 180 nm channel hole lined with polysilicon through 100 LPCVD-deposited gate layers (hole etched with 1990s deep-trench AR ~40); a sense node at the pillar top reads packets in sequence, ~50 bits per pillar.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): one 180 nm mask defines holes while film thickness sets vertical pitch, ~0.003 um2/bit footprint (near 12 nm DRAM) with zero EUV; ~50 ns average shift latency; risk is transfer efficiency in poly channels.

title: Po: every bit is a battery — electromotive-force readout micro-cells
idea: Po: every bit is a battery. Extracted: each crossbar crossing is a sputtered solid-state sodium micro-cell (iron-phosphate cathode, no cobalt); the bit is its open-circuit voltage (4 levels = 2 bits), read potentiometrically at near-zero current (non-destructive) and written with an nA charge pulse.
why: A cell holds state with no transistor to leak through, so a transistorless sputtered 64-layer crossbar aims 100x lower $/GB. Trade-offs: us-ms writes and finite cycle life unless shallow cycling stays reversible.

title: Nanobattery voltage-mode bit read potentiometrically, signal independent of size
idea: EV battery managers read cell voltage, not charge; likewise each bit is a solid-state micro-battery (LixTiO2/LiPON-like stack) whose open-circuit voltage differs by ~0.3 V between states, sensed by a high-impedance FET gate. A battery's voltage does not shrink with its area, so the read signal survives scaling where capacitor charge does not.
why: Sidesteps the capacitor charge wall entirely (fact 1); quasi-non-volatile with no refresh; ion kinetics (us) and cycle life are the obstacles.

title: Vertical Bloch line memory revived with DMI-tuned stripe domains
idea: NEC's 1983 VBL memory stored bits as pairs of vertical Bloch lines inside the walls of stripe domains, features far smaller than bubbles. Revive it in [Pt/Co/Ir] multilayers whose interfacial DMI is tuned near the Neel-Bloch crossover so Bloch-line pairs are stable at ~10-nm pitch, shifted along walls by in-plane current pulses and read where the wall end meets an MTJ.
why: Bits defined by topology, not litho: ~10x skyrmion-track density potential (Tb/in2 class) with no transistor or capacitor per bit (Facts 1, 2, 4).

title: Separate capacitor wafer hybrid-bonded to transistor wafer at cell pitch
idea: Combine deep-trench decoupling-capacitor manufacturing (mature, DUV-only) with sub-500 nm pitch wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding: one wafer carries only dense trench capacitors, the other carries access transistors and periphery, and each cell's storage node is joined by a Cu-Cu pad. Each wafer is optimized and yield-screened separately, and the capacitor wafer can come from a low-capital U.S. MEMS or passive-component fab.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability (facts 4, 7): no EUV in the capacitor flow and parallel fabs; claimed 20-30% wafer cost cut; bond pitch and overlay are the risks.

title: Pop-up toaster: telescoping nested nanotube held extended or retracted
idea: Stimulus 'pop-up toaster' -> a double-walled carbon nanotube whose inner tube slides out of the outer one; an electrostatic pull extends it to touch a contact pad (bit 1), and the van der Waals retraction force plus a reverse pulse pulls it back (bit 0). Read is contact current; the shell-in-shell sliding is superlubric, so there is no bending fatigue.
why: Zero-leakage nonvolatile mechanical bit (fact 3) with near-frictionless motion for high endurance; vertical tubes stack in BEOL with no capacitor (facts 1-2).

title: Persistent-current flux bits cooled by cryocoolers, not helium
idea: Invert 'bits must live in charge or polarization of matter' -> store them as a quantized persistent current. NbN or MgB2 nanowire loops hold one flux quantum clockwise or counter-clockwise with zero dissipation, written by kinetic-inductance switching and read by a nanowire cryotron, cooled by closed-cycle cryocoolers instead of liquid helium.
why: Zero static power, unlimited endurance and ~10 aJ switching (fact 10), fitting cryogenic AI accelerators; avoids the Qatar helium chokepoint; density and ~400 W/W 4 K overhead (MgB2 at 20 K cuts it ~10x) are the risks.

title: Self-dissolving silver nanocluster bit with designed one-second lifetime
idea: In an RT-sputtered SiOxNy:Ag diffusive layer, a write pulse nucleates a sub-2 nm Ag bridge that conducts ~uA. Gibbs-Thomson surface energy then dissolves it with tau set by cluster size and matrix diffusivity, designed at ~1 s, and refresh rewrites it.
why: Dissolution kinetics replace capacitor leakage as the retention clock, with a uA gain-like read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). Avoids permanent oxygen-vacancy damage, targeting 1e10+ endurance versus ReRAM's ~1e6.

title: Contactless snap-through nanomembrane: bistable mechanical bit, vacuum-insulated
idea: Scarcity rule: vacuum is the only insulator allowed. A pre-buckled SiN or few-layer-graphene membrane over a sealed 20 nm cavity has two stable shapes; an electrostatic pulse from a bottom electrode snaps it up or down, and one access transistor senses the capacitance difference. It never touches anything, so there is no stiction or contact wear.
why: Zero leakage and zero hold power (fact 3) at GHz mechanical resonance for sub-100 nm membranes; elastic bending below 1% strain gives effectively unlimited cycles.

title: Photosynthetic cascade trap: stepped wells carry electrons out of reach
idea: Reaction centres prevent charge recombination by hopping the electron down a chain of acceptors, each step further away. Build the storage node as a graded staircase of 3-4 oxide-semiconductor quantum wells (e.g. IGZO/Ga2O3/ZnMgO with stepped conduction-band offsets) beside a transistor channel. A write pulse cascades electrons into the far well, where back-tunneling is exponentially suppressed by distance, shifting Vt non-volatilely; an opposite low-field pulse reverses the cascade.
why: Non-volatile charge storage at low write field (~0.3 V steps instead of ~10 MV/cm Fowler-Nordheim tunneling), aiming at 10^9-10^12 endurance and ~50 ns writes. BEOL oxide process, no EUV.

title: Threshold-switch-gated crosspoint capacitor without access transistor
idea: MINIFY the cell to a 4F2 crosspoint: each capacitor is in series with a Mott threshold switch (NbO2 or doped VOx) that is insulating below ~0.8 V and conducting above, so only fully selected cells charge or discharge while half-selected ones stay sealed; decks stack 8+ high using only deposition and line patterning.
why: No transistor, monolithic 3D stacking (fact 2) on mature-litho lines (fact 4); threshold-switch off-leakage may limit retention to ms.

title: Po: the worst transistor is the best — cryo poly-Si 3D stack
idea: Po: the worst transistor is the best. Extracted: build 128-tier 1T1C stacks with cheap, leaky low-temperature poly-Si TFT access devices using a NAND-like single-hole etch and no EUV, then run the module at ~150 K where trap-assisted leakage drops by orders of magnitude, turning unusable cells into seconds-retention DRAM.
why: Accepting a cryocooler unlocks the cheapest 3D flow (near NAND cost, ~100x below DRAM contract) and also lowers wire resistance. Trade-offs: cooling power and cold packaging.

title: Swap electron storage for proton position in hydrated-oxide gate
idea: A 3-terminal cell shuttles H+ between a Pd-H reservoir and a WO3 channel through a 5 nm phosphosilicate-glass proton conductor. Pulses of ~5 ns at ~1 V (as in MIT's protonic resistors) set the channel conductance, which is read non-destructively.
why: Retention of hours to days cuts refresh (fact 3) and non-destructive read helps fact 8. The films are deposition-defined at DUV pitch, and protons need no scarce elements.

title: Geiger-mode avalanche read of a hundred-electron storage node
idea: Shrink the storage node to ~20 aF holding ~100 electrons and wire it as the bias of a SPAD-like junction. At read the junction is armed above breakdown for ~2 ns: a stored '1' tips it into avalanche (gain ~1e5) and a '0' does not, then an active quench resets it.
why: Poisson statistics need only N >= 36 electrons for 6-sigma discrimination, and kT/C noise on 20 aF is ~2 electrons rms. Storing 31,000 electrons is an artifact of bitline charge sharing, so the capacitor shrinks ~50x, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1) and 1-2 patterning layers (fact 4).

title: Few-electron storage read by single-electron transistor for smart dust
idea: Millimeter smart-dust nodes cannot afford 30,000-electron capacitors, so a 5-10 nm Si island stores ~50-200 electrons and an adjacent room-temperature single-electron transistor converts each added electron into a large current swing. The storage element shrinks to aF-scale capacitance with no pillar.
why: Removes the charge wall (fact 1) and cuts write energy ~100x (fact 10); room-temperature SET variability and background offset charges are the barrier.

title: Access transistor turns avalanche amplifier during the read window
idea: Reverse the access device's job on read: for a 1 ns window its drain junction is biased just above breakdown, so the few hundred electrons released from a tiny 0.1 fF node trigger quenched impact-ionization gain of ~100 (SPAD-like) and produce a full-swing bitline signal; at idle it is a normal off transistor.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): Cs can shrink ~50x to a planar capacitor while keeping sense margin; risks are avalanche noise, dark counts and hot-carrier wear.

title: Antiferroelectric charge-step capacitor that pins voltage against leakage
idea: Worsen: demand ever more charge from a linear dielectric, forcing AR 115:1 pillars. Flip: use an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich HZO film with the plate biased so a stored '1' sits just above the AFE-to-FE transition; the switching charge adds ~2-3x Q per area, and as leakage pulls the node down the film releases bound charge, creating a voltage plateau that stretches retention.
why: Fact 1 charge wall: the same Cs at AR ~25-30:1 instead of 60-75:1; the plateau effect could roughly double retention time (fact 3).

title: Multi-electron redox molecules as pseudocapacitive storage for printed sensors
idea: Disposable printed sensors need cheap memory, so the storage electrode carries a self-assembled monolayer of porphyrin/ferrocene multi-redox molecules that each hold 2-4 electrons at distinct potentials, giving 5-10x the charge per area of a dielectric capacitor. Charging through short molecular tethers takes tens of ns and the distinct redox levels allow 2 bits per cell.
why: Faradaic pseudocapacitance beats the dielectric charge wall (fact 1) without high aspect ratio and adds multi-level storage; molecular stability over 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Liquid-nitrogen immersed DRAM racks where retention outlasts data
idea: Combine LN2 immersion cooling (already used for HTS cables and extreme overclocking) with commodity DRAM pools: at 77 K access-transistor leakage falls by many orders of magnitude, stretching retention from 64 ms to hours, so refresh is simply switched off. Cryo also speeds transistors ~20% and cuts wire resistance several-fold.
why: Zero refresh power and 10-20% bandwidth recovered; cooling overhead (~10 W input per W removed at 77 K) must be amortized at disaggregated memory-pool scale.

title: Polarization-bound GaN quantum-well charge storage for 200C downhole tools
idea: Oil-well logging tools need memory at 200C; an AlN/GaN/AlN double heterostructure forms a 2DEG well bounded by 6.2 eV AlN barriers and fixed polarization charge, so an injected electron sheet barely emits thermally. The stored sheet modulates an adjacent HEMT channel for non-destructive read, built in existing U.S. 200 mm GaN-on-Si power fabs.
why: Ultra-wide barriers cut leakage >1e6x vs Si junctions, giving seconds-to-hours room-temperature retention (fact 3) without a capacitor (fact 1), on U.S.-available GaN capacity (manufacturability).

title: Ramtron FeRAM revived with non-destructive piezoelectric-sign readout
idea: Early 1T1C PZT FeRAM suffered destructive reads and fatigue. On existing 130-nm FRAM lines that already integrate PZT, read polarization by applying a small AC voltage and sensing the sign of the resulting piezoelectric strain with a capacitive or piezoresistive sense layer over the capacitor, as piezoresponse microscopy does.
why: Removes destructive read and write-back (Fact 8: ~50% read energy) and the fatigue cycles they cause; non-volatile (Fact 3); existing FRAM capacity.

title: One contact for eight bits: NAND-chained capacitor strings
idea: Rearrange cells from parallel to series: chain eight 180 nm 1T1C cells with one bitline contact (as in early-1990s NAND-structured DRAM proposals), read them destructively in fixed order from the contact end and write back in reverse order, so contacts no longer set cell area.
why: Density and periphery (facts 4,7): cell area falls toward 4F2 as seven of eight contacts vanish; sequential access suits page-streaming AI workloads; risk is far-cell latency.

title: Si: Coulomb-blockaded 3 nm silicon dot holds exact electron counts
idea: Shrink the storage node to a ~3 nm silicon dot whose single-electron charging energy (>100 meV, far above kT) blocks tunneling unless the gate is pulsed; the bit is 0 or N electrons, so leakage becomes a rare discrete event instead of a continuous drain, read by an integrated single-electron transistor.
why: Turns the access-leakage tail (fact 3) into Coulomb-gap-suppressed escape and lets the node scale to atomic size (fact 4); room-temperature dot-size variability is the risk.

title: STT barrier wear-out turned self-healing with spinel MgAl2O4
idea: STT-MRAM as DRAM failed partly because write currents build oxygen-vacancy traps in MgO until breakdown (~1e10-1e12 cycles). Use a lattice-matched spinel MgAl2O4 barrier, cation-disorder engineered so vacancy traps anneal out at 125 C or below within hours, so a hot ambient repairs the barrier faster than writes damage it.
why: Turns 125 C from a stressor into a continuous healing anneal, potentially lifting endurance toward 1e15 for DRAM-class duty.

title: Swap EUV masks for maskless two-beam interference lattice exposure
idea: Memory arrays are periodic, so expose the capacitor and wordline lattices by 193-nm immersion two-beam interference (~40 nm pitch per pass). Double exposure with the grating rotated forms the hole lattice, and a cheap DUV trim mask cuts the array edges.
why: Replaces EUV for the dense periodic layers (fact 4) with a simpler, cheaper interference tool that needs no mask set and could be built in the U.S.

title: Parametron phase bits held by a shared resonant pump
idea: Invert 'a bit is a static stored quantity' -> the bit is the phase (0 or pi) of a sustained sub-harmonic oscillation. On-die high-Q LC or AlN bulk-acoustic parametrons are pumped at 2f by one shared resonant clock tree; each locks into one of two phases, written by a tiny seed injection and read by mixing against a reference phase.
why: Removes the capacitor charge wall and refresh entirely (facts 1, 3): the pump regenerates every bit every cycle and the resonant tree recycles most pump energy; standby cost scales with 1/Q rather than leakage tails.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits held by bias light
idea: Shift storage into photon lifetime: an InP photonic-crystal nanocavity with carrier-plasma bistability sits on a shared continuous bias beam, and the bit is the high or low intracavity energy state; a pulse flips it.
why: Data movement: memory lives in the optical domain beside photonic interconnect, with ~fJ switching.

title: Panel-scale memory on Gen-8.5 glass using nanoimprint
idea: Because nothing exceeds 400 C, build a planar oxide or ferroic storage array on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass in display-type panel lines, patterned by roll-to-plate nanoimprint at ~30 nm with ~4 stacked tiers. Each panel has ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
why: Panel cost per m2 is ~10-20x below wafer cost, attacking capital intensity and cost per bit. Panel lines can be built in the U.S. faster than DRAM fabs.

title: Po: the wordlines are made of sound — acoustic coincidence-addressed array
idea: Po: the wordlines are made of sound. Extracted: replace row and column drivers with two edge transducers launching surface-acoustic-wave pulses across a piezoelectric-semiconductor film; only where two pulses cross does the summed strain lower a storage node's barrier enough to exchange charge with a blanket electrode, selecting one cell by time of flight.
why: Removes per-row/column decoders and drivers (periphery ~49%, fact 7) and most array metal, aiming at 100x cheaper per GB. Trade-offs: us access and acoustic crosstalk.

title: Tuareg sealed jar: Ga2O3 gain cell patterned through stencil masks
idea: A Tuareg potter seals water in a jar so none seeps out. A 2-transistor gain cell uses sputtered amorphous Ga2O3 channels (4.8 eV gap) with off-currents of ~1e-22 A, so charge stays for days. Reusable silicon-nitride stencil masks pattern the BEOL array, so those layers need no resist, develop, strip or post-etch clean.
why: Days of retention all but switches off refresh (fact 3), with a wider gap than IGZO. Stencil patterning removes the litho-track and wet-strip water for the storage layers, cutting UPW by more than 10x.

title: Eliminate the separate capacitor: ferroelectric-semiconductor channel stores the bit itself
idea: Eliminate both the capacitor and the gate stack: make the channel from a ~3-nm ferroelectric semiconductor (alpha-In2Se3) whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization modulates its own conductance by 1e3-1e5, so one device is both storage and access, with a non-destructive read.
why: Collapses 1T1C into one ~4F2 device, removing the capacitor wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3); stackable in BEOL below 400 C; risk is retention and endurance beyond 1e12 cycles.

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel: the transistor itself is the bit
idea: Effect walk: locked in-plane/out-of-plane ferroelectricity in a semiconductor. A 3-nm alpha-In2Se3 channel's own polarization sets its band bending and conductance; a ~0.5 V gate pulse switches the channel dipoles, and reading at 0.1 V drain bias senses a ~10^3 current ratio without disturbing polarization.
why: No separate capacitor or full-swing bitline: a 0.1-V gain read gives ~10-20x lower read energy than DRAM sensing and avoids destructive read (fact 8); indium supply concentration is a resource caveat.

title: Spin-echo storage revived: electron-spin ensembles as phase-coded bit trains
idea: In 1955 Anderson and Fernbach proposed computer memories that store data in spin precession phases and recall them with a refocusing pulse. Couple ensembles of donor electron spins in isotopically pure 28Si:P to on-chip microwave resonators so each resonator holds a train of thousands of time-multiplexed, phase-encoded bits recalled as echoes.
why: No transistor or capacitor per bit and time multiplexing puts thousands of bits on one resonator; spin coherence of seconds dwarfs 64 ms; needs cryogenic operation, so speculative.

title: Eliminate the solid channel: vacuum field-emission access to storage nodes
idea: Eliminate solid-state leakage: connect each storage node through a sealed 10-nm vacuum nano-gap with a sharp field-emission tip; at hold bias the Fowler-Nordheim current is effectively zero because there is no semiconductor and no generation, while a few-volt access pulse across the gap conducts uA in picoseconds.
why: Retention limited only by dielectric leakage (hours), so refresh disappears (fact 3); radiation hard; risks are tip wear, work-function drift and 3-5 V access voltage (fact 10).

title: Nano-DMD torsion latch: Texas micromirror physics shrunk to memory bits
idea: Box = {medium: landed-left or landed-right state of a 100 nm torsion-hinge paddle | access: row/column electrostatic half-select | sense: capacitive tilt sensing | integration: MEMS over CMOS as in DLP | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the Dallas DLP flow (Al hinges, SAM anti-stiction, spring tips)}. A small hold bias keeps the paddle latched on its landing tip; DLP mirrors already pass 1e12 landings with stiction controlled, and shrinking ~50x raises the resonance to GHz for ns switching.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no charge leakage and no destructive read; an existing domestic MEMS base becomes memory capacity.

title: Vacuum-gap floating node written by field emission
idea: Worsen: store charge behind oxides whose traps leak and wear out. Flip: put the storage node on a nanoscale island isolated by a sealed 3-5 nm vacuum gap; writes use field emission across the gap, and retention relies on vacuum, which has no traps, no stress-induced leakage and no wear.
why: Removes the trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3) and floating-gate endurance limits; a candidate refresh-free node.

title: Musician hears four pitches: self-referenced 4-level DRAM cell
idea: A musician hears four notes where an engineer hears 'high or low'. Store four charge levels in a standard capacitor, and pair every 64 cells with a reference cell written in the same burst. The sense amp compares against a twin that has leaked by the same amount (relative pitch) instead of a fixed threshold.
why: 2 bits per cell doubles density per wafer (fact 4), and references that track drift tolerate the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Beetle-cuticle ferroelectric nematic: fluid polar bit that cannot fatigue
idea: Beetle cuticles and cell membranes are biological liquid crystals. Fill 20 nm cells with a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734-class, polarization ~6 uC/cm2) between electrodes whose polar surface anchoring makes both polarization directions stable. A field reorients the fluid to write, and the switching current reads the bit, as in FeRAM.
why: Non-volatile, with intrinsically unlimited endurance because a fluid has no lattice defects to fatigue. Switches below 1 V at 20 nm and is filled from solution.

title: Photo film: silver-bromide latent-image speck as an atom-scale bit
idea: Stimulus 'silver-halide film' -> a 10 nm AgBr nanocrystal between two electrodes: an electron pulse nucleates a 4-atom Ag cluster (the photographic latent image) at a sensitivity site, making the crystal tunnel-conductive; an oxidizing pulse dissolves it. Bromide chemistry, no fluorine.
why: Few-atom motion promises lower energy and variability than filamentary ReRAM; nonvolatile so no refresh (fact 3); low-temperature halide deposition fits BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Photochromic-lens diarylethene switched electrically as the storage molecule
idea: Adapt Transitions-lens photochromics: diarylethene molecules ring-close or ring-open on a redox pulse, changing conductance ~100x; a monolayer between nanogap electrodes stores the bit as molecular conformation.
why: Fact 3 and density: conformation needs no stored charge, so retention is set by a ~1 eV isomer barrier rather than leakage, at molecular footprint.

title: A magnet with no magnetization: Mn3Sn Weyl antiferromagnet bits
idea: Reverse ferromagnet thinking: store the bit in the chiral spin order of a noncollinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn) with ~zero net moment, toggled by spin-orbit torque and read through its large Berry-curvature anomalous Hall voltage rather than through magnetization.
why: Density, speed and refresh (fact 3): zero stray field lets cells pack below 20 nm pitch without coupling, ps-scale dynamics, nonvolatile; risk is small Hall signal at tiny sizes.

title: Ferreed crosspoint revived: nanomagnet-latched NEMS contact as the bit
idea: Bell's 1960 ferreed latched a reed contact with a remanent magnet. Shrink it to a 100-nm NEMS cantilever with a CoPt hard-magnet tip that latches onto a soft-magnetic pad when the pad is magnetized parallel and springs open when antiparallel; a current-strap pulse flips the pad to write, and contact conduction (on/off >1e8) reads.
why: Bit held magnetically (non-volatile, no refresh, Fact 3) while the readout is a mechanical switch with near-infinite on/off ratio, so it self-selects in a crosspoint with no transistor or selector (Facts 2, 7); aJ-class read.

title: Dynamic copper-filament crosspoint memory refreshed like DRAM
idea: Box = {medium: volatile nanoscale Cu filament in SiO2 that dissolves over ~1 s | access: none (self-rectifying stack) | sense: filament on/off current ~1e3 | integration: 4F2 crosspoint stacked 8 layers | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered Arizona copper + PECVD SiO2}. Filaments are kept deliberately thin so they relax on their own, which allows low compliance current and longer endurance, and a 1 s refresh rewrites the ones.
why: Density (4F2 x 8 layers) and capital: a crosspoint with no access transistor, built from only Cu, Si and O.

title: Po: the whole bit is one electron — room-temperature silicon dot box
idea: Po: the whole bit is one electron. Extracted: a sub-3 nm Si nanocrystal embedded in an oxide pillar has Coulomb charging energy >10 kT at 300 K; the bit is n vs n+1 electrons, sensed through the gate of a nanowire channel, with retention set by an energy gap rather than by charge volume.
why: Bit charge ~1000x smaller than 5 fF, collapsing CV2 energy (fact 10). Dot-size uniformity is the risk.

title: Swap linear dielectric for antiferroelectric charge-burst capacitor dielectric
idea: Replace the ZrO2/Al2O3 linear cap dielectric with a field-induced antiferroelectric (ZrO2-rich HfZrO or Pb-free NaNbO3-based) whose AFE-to-FE transition sits just below the write voltage, so writing a '1' adds the released polarization (~15-25 uC/cm2) to the linear charge. At zero field the film relaxes back to the non-polar phase, so there is no remanent imprint and the cell stays a volatile DRAM cell.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 2-3x stored charge per pillar at today's AR ~60:1, or the same 5 fF at AR ~25:1, which also makes 3D tiers easier.

title: Vacuum-sealed storage node with field-emission nanogap access switch
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): suspend each storage node on thin oxide posts inside a sealed nano-vacuum cavity so no junction or dielectric film touches it, and access it through a gated vacuum-channel field-emission diode with a <50-nm gap that conducts only above its turn-on field. Vacuum has no traps or band tails, so hold leakage is set by Fowler-Nordheim at low field (aA-class).
why: Fact 3: refresh intervals of minutes to hours; the vacuum switch's extremely steep turn-on also helps fact 10.

title: Williams tube reborn: field-emitter array writes charge spots on continuous film
idea: Revive the 1947 Williams tube (the first DRAM) with field-emission-display Spindt tip arrays: in a vacuum-sealed package each tip is electrostatically deflected over a 4x4 patch to write and read charge spots on an unpatterned SiO2 electret film over a sense grid, reading by secondary-emission contrast. The storage plane needs no per-bit transistor, capacitor or lithography.
why: Facts 4 and 7: the storage plane is a blanket film, so patterned features per bit drop ~16x (16 bits per tip); charge on high-quality oxide in vacuum leaks negligibly; vacuum packaging and tip lifetime are the risks.

title: Weather vane rotors: dipolar molecular rotors locked in crystalline cages
idea: Amphidynamic crystals and MOFs hold polar rotors (e.g., difluorophenylene on a rigid axle) that point like weather vanes; engineer a two-fold rotational potential with ~0.8-1.0 eV barrier, grow an oriented 10-nm MOF film as the cell dielectric, and switch rotor orientation with a field pulse so the net polarization shifts a readout capacitance or channel threshold.
why: Ferroelectric-like non-volatility without oxide fatigue, since each rotor flips independently with no vacancy-pinned domain walls, and the barrier is chemically tunable; the speed-versus-retention trade is unproven.

title: Mood-ring molecules: spin-crossover film switches capacitance bistably
idea: Like a mood ring, Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 10-30 K hysteresis loop near room temperature and a large dielectric and volume change; thermally evaporate or spin-coat a 10-nm film between Pt electrodes, park the die inside the loop, write with a ns field/Joule pulse, and read the capacitance shift.
why: Non-volatile inside the loop with no ion migration, and switching has been shown on ns optical timescales; needs only an evaporator, spin coater and e-beam; endurance and a narrow thermal window are the risks.

title: Hot-foil stamping bit: single heat pulse toggles a GdFeCo magnet
idea: A hot-foil stamp transfers its image with one heat pulse. In the same way, a ~10 ps current pulse heats a GdFeCo ferrimagnet nanodot, and ultrafast Gd/Fe sublattice exchange toggles its magnetization with no field, no spin torque and no polarity. An MTJ on top reads it.
why: DRAM-class (ps) write speed in a nonvolatile cell with unlimited endurance. Simple toggle drivers cut refresh and periphery (facts 3 and 7).

title: Contactless coupled storage dies lift off for replacement
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension + #28 Mechanics substitution: stack storage dies with no TSVs or hybrid bonds; signals cross by inductive/capacitive coupling (~0.1 pJ/bit), power arrives through a few spring micro-contacts, and a reversible clamp holds the stack, so a worn storage die is lifted out and replaced while the logic base die stays.
why: Fact 6: avoids the HBM TSV tax (~3x area per bit, 20-30% yield loss) and allows known-good-die replacement instead of scrapping whole stacks.

title: On-chip gigahertz phononic delay loop recirculating bits in flight
idea: MAGNIFY frequency and MINIFY wavelength of 1940s mercury delay-line memory: 20 GHz acoustic pulses travel ~4 km/s in thin-film LiNbO3 or AlScN waveguides, so a 1-mm spiral holds ~5 us x 20 Gb/s = 100 kbit, regenerated by a piezo transducer and comparator at each loop end.
why: ~1e8 bit/mm2 with no cell, no capacitor and no EUV (facts 1, 4); energy only spent regenerating; suits sequential tiers such as streaming KV caches.

title: Magnetostrictive delay line reborn as recirculating spin-wave registers
idea: 1950s calculators stored bits as acoustic pulses in magnetostrictive nickel wire. Store bits instead as ~5 GHz spin-wave packets in permalloy/CoFeB waveguide loops patterned on an existing 180-nm line, with inductive antennas and a CMOS amplifier regenerating each loop every pass.
why: Bit is a wave in flight: no cell, no capacitor; ~1-um bit spacing gives ~0.1-1 Mb/mm2 and 10-50 ns latency in short loops for FIFO/KV-cache streaming buffers; regeneration energy is the open risk.

title: Knitted MgB2 persistent-current loops for a cryogenic memory tier
idea: Interlock superconducting MgB2 loops like knitting (Tc 39 K, Mg and B only). Each loop holds a bit as a circulating persistent current, a flux quantum in or out, switched and sensed by an MgB2 nano-bridge, forming a 20 K cryocooled memory tier beside cryogenic AI accelerators.
why: Facts 3 and 10: zero static power, no refresh and aJ switching, ~1e6x below DRAM write energy. Cryocooler capital buys freedom from exotic metals.

title: Organic food label: certified fluorine-free memory gets procurement and permit advantage
idea: Stimulus 'organic food label' -> create a U.S. 'PFAS-free memory' certification (no PFAS resists or surfactants, no fluorinated etch or clean, no WF6) tied to federal procurement preference and fast-track water permits, because fluorine-free fabs skip PFAS wastewater treatment and clear the coming EU PFAS restriction. It pulls the fluorine-free storage elements in this cell into early demand.
why: Turns the constraint into market access and faster fab siting (capital and time chokepoints); estimated $100M+ abatement capex avoided per fab and EU export de-risked.

title: 1952 BaTiO3 crossbar redone in AlScN: square loop, Tc >1000 C
idea: Bell Labs' 1952 BaTiO3 matrix memory failed because its rounded loop let half-select pulses disturb neighbours, and its ~120 C Curie point sits right at 125 C. Wurtzite Al0.7Sc0.3N switches through nucleation-limited, very square loops (Ec ~3-5 MV/cm), so a passive V/3 crossbar is disturb-free, and its polarization is safe far above 125 C because its Tc exceeds 1000 C.
why: Transistor-free stackable crosspoint FeRAM that qualifies at Grade 1 (125 C/10 y); ~4F2 per layer; lead-free, sputtered with CMOS-compatible tools.

title: Memory wallpaper: square metres of printed foil DRAM
idea: IFR: memory as cheap per area as a solar panel. Closest achievable: print 1T1C oxide-TFT cells at 2 um pitch on PV-grade foil (~2.5e7 bits/cm^2, ~30 GB per m^2 at ~$50/m^2) and mount panels as a capacity tier behind HBM/DDR.
why: Cost per bit (~$2/GB) and capital (PV-class lines) at the price of us-class latency; adds supply outside DRAM fabs.

title: Laminated van der Waals capacitor stacks instead of deep etching
idea: Worsen: get capacitance only by etching 75:1 holes. Flip: build area by laminating 20-50 alternating graphene/hBN sheets into an interdigitated parallel-plate stack contacted on staircased edges, so capacitance scales with layer count rather than etch depth.
why: Avoids high-AR etch (fact 1) and tungsten fills; atomically flat hBN has very low leakage.

title: Butterfly-scale gyroid capacitor from block-copolymer self-assembly
idea: Green hairstreak butterfly scales grow a single-gyroid photonic network. Spin a double-gyroid block-copolymer film (~20 nm period) as a sacrificial template, ALD-fill one network with TiN, strip the polymer, coat with high-k, and fill the second network as the counter-electrode. The two interpenetrating continuous electrodes give a 3D capacitor with ~30-60x area per footprint in a 300 nm layer.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1, 4): spin-coat self-assembly replaces the AR-70 pillar etch and the support-mesh steps. Each cell is isolated by a shallow cut, not a deep etch.

title: JEDEC 'one-second class' standard unlocking low-barrier memory elements
idea: Standardize a memory class with 1 s retention at 85 C, >=1e16 endurance and mandatory on-die ECC scrub. Barrier height = ln(retention/attempt time) kT, so emerging elements (MRAM, FeRAM, ReRAM) can be designed at ~28 kT instead of 60 kT, trading unneeded retention for write energy and endurance.
why: Write energy and wear scale with barrier height, so halving it gives new storage physics a qualified path to fill DRAM sockets now, raising usable supply.

title: Printed spin-crossover film held inside its room-temperature hysteresis
idea: IFR: a molecule that remembers its spin state at no cost. Closest achievable: print [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)]-class nanoparticles with a ~40 K wide hysteresis loop, hold the array at mid-loop temperature, set high-spin with a ns local heat pulse and low-spin with a piezo strain pulse, and read the ~10% volume/dielectric change.
why: Nonvolatile within the operating window, molecular switching with no wear, all-printed; write energy is the risk.

title: Core-plane separation: universal 28-nm periphery die bonded to revived arrays
idea: Core memories separated the passive core plane from shared drive and sense electronics. Split every revived storage array (magnetic, mechanical, charge) from a standard 28-nm sense/IO die hybrid-bonded wafer-to-wafer on existing CIS-fab bonding lines, with a programmable sense front end (current, voltage, inductive, phase).
why: Periphery is ~49% of DRAM die (Fact 7); moving it to a cheap mature-node die makes arrays ~100% array and lets any exotic element reach a DDR/CXL interface without its own PHY.

title: Eliminate dielectric deposition: anodically grow the capacitor dielectric from its electrode
idea: Eliminate the deposited dielectric: form a Nb or Ta bottom electrode by CVD or electroless plating, then anodize it so a dense Nb2O5 (k~40) or Ta2O5 (k~25) film grows inward at ~2 nm/V, perfectly conformal at any aspect ratio, with thickness set by voltage to ~0.1 nm. No plasma, no sputter targets and no rare-gas ALD purges are used.
why: Conformality at AR >100 is automatic (fact 1) and the dielectric tool is a wet cell (fact 4); anodic growth thickens fastest at weak spots, trimming the leakage tail (fact 3); risk is lower k than the best ZAZ stacks at equal leakage.

title: Stiction-latched graphene nanorelay held by van der Waals force
idea: Worsen: hold the bit with a charge that leaks. Flip: hold it with adhesion: an exfoliated few-layer graphene cantilever snaps onto a contact and stays stuck by van der Waals force until a reverse pulse peels it off; build 100 devices in a university lab in 12 months and spend the next 12 on cycling.
why: Zero leakage, zero standby power, no refresh (fact 3), for under $500k.

title: Ferroelectric semiconductor channel: alpha-In2Se3 holds bit in itself
idea: Fuse channel and storage element: alpha-In2Se3 is a 2D semiconductor whose own lattice is ferroelectric, so switching its polarization changes the channel conductance directly. A one-transistor cell with no gate ferroelectric and no capacitor stores the bit in the channel and reads it non-destructively.
why: Zero refresh in a 1T 4F2 cell without the interface-trap fatigue of FeFET gate stacks; indium supply and 2D growth uniformity are risks.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass fabs building IGZO capacitor memory panels
idea: Combine display-panel manufacturing (Gen-10.5 glass, 2-3 um lines, IGZO backplanes already in volume) with 1T1C memory: pattern memory arrays across square meters of glass at roughly a cent per cm2, then cut them into large capacity-tier panels attached by flex to CXL controllers. It trades density for ~1000x cheaper area and zero EUV.
why: Capital and scarce tools (fact 4): uses idle display capacity outside the EUV supply chain; cost per bit could approach parity for capacity tiers; latency, RC and physical size are the risks.

title: Conveyor-belt sushi: bits ride recirculating gigahertz phonon loops
idea: Stimulus 'sushi conveyor' -> store data as acoustic pulses circulating in short on-chip AlN acoustic loops (64 bits per ~1.3 ns, ~10 um loop), regenerated by a tiny amplifier each lap, like a mercury delay line made micro. Sound is ~10^5x slower than light, so a micron-scale loop holds a cache line with no capacitor or access transistor.
why: Capacitor-free, transistor-light storage with no leakage tail (fact 3) built on mature-node, EUV-free lines (fact 4); periphery shrinks to one amplifier per 64 bits (fact 7); density is lower, so it targets capital-light capacity tiers.

title: Seashell nacre: titania nanosheets self-stack into a k~125 dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'nacre' (layered bricks of mineral) -> exfoliate Ti0.87O2 nanosheets in water with tetrabutylammonium hydroxide and deposit them layer by layer by Langmuir-Blodgett at room temperature, giving a ~5 nm dielectric with k~125 and low leakage; no plasma, no fluorinated surfactants.
why: k~125 exceeds the k~70 needed (fact 1), letting capacitor AR fall to ~40:1; room-temperature aqueous deposition lowers tool capex (fact 4).

title: Logic-die decoupling capacitors double as on-demand scratch memory
idea: Invert 'storage elements must be dedicated memory cells' -> reuse the capacitors already on every logic die. An accelerator's deep-trench/MIM decap is split into ~50 fF segments with access switches, so idle decap banks act as eDRAM-like scratch when the supply-noise budget allows and revert to decoupling during load surges.
why: ~15% of an 800 mm^2 die at ~500 nF/mm^2 is ~1e9 storable bits (~100+ MB) of near-compute memory with ~zero added wafer area, cutting data-movement energy (fact 5) and DRAM demand.

title: PERC solar back side: negative-charge Al2O3 fences carriers from storage node
idea: PERC solar cells use ALD Al2O3 carrying ~1e13 cm-2 negative fixed charge to repel minority carriers from surfaces; wrap storage-node junction sidewalls and isolation liners in 5-nm ALD Al2O3 so the field pushes the generation-active depletion edge away from defective interfaces, followed by forming-gas hydrogenation, demonstrated on university test diodes and gated capacitors.
why: Fact 3: perimeter interface generation dominates the leakage tail, so ~10x lower perimeter generation gives ~3-10x longer worst-cell retention using only ALD and a furnace.

title: Seesaw: negative-capacitance layer amplifies the storage capacitor
idea: Stimulus 'seesaw' (push one end down, the other rises) -> place a 3 nm ZrO2-based ferroelectric, biased in its negative-capacitance region, in series with an Al2O3/ZrO2 storage dielectric, all ALD from ZrCl4 and TMA/H2O; the dielectric stabilizes the stack so it shows no hysteresis while net capacitance exceeds the dielectric alone.
why: Raises Cs ~1.5-2x at the same AR (fact 1) or lets the array voltage drop for the same charge (fact 10); chloride/organometallic ALD only, no fluorine.

title: Order-disorder molecular-rotor ferroelectric printed below 150 C
idea: Print a molecular ferroelectric (diisopropylammonium bromide or imidazolium perchlorate class, Pr 10-20 uC/cm2, Tc >400 K) as the final tier. Polarization comes from whole cationic dipoles rotating in place rather than ions hopping through vacancies, and ~1 V pulses write it.
why: Rotation should avoid vacancy-driven fatigue (endurance) and gives ~10x a linear dielectric's charge per area (fact 1), processed at <=150 C from earth-abundant C/H/N/Br.

title: Namib fog beetle: area-selective evaporated molecular ferroelectric dots
idea: The Namib beetle collects water only on the bumps of its back. Patterned nucleation spots make a molecular ferroelectric (diisopropylammonium bromide class: order-disorder cations, Pr ~20 uC/cm2, Tc >420 K) condense from vapor only where cells sit, so the storage layer never needs lithography, etch or clean.
why: Self-aligned, non-volatile polar storage (facts 1, 3) with no mask for that layer (fact 4). The storage module has no wet steps, a more than 10x water cut.

title: Grown carbon-nanotube forest capacitors replacing etched pillars
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric coating a 30 nm vertically aligned CNT bundle | access: vertical Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: DSA-patterned Fe catalyst dots (Minnesota iron) + CVD growth from U.S. natural-gas methane}. Each cell's electrode grows 3 um tall from its catalyst dot instead of being etched, giving surface area beyond AR 100:1 without any high-AR plasma etch.
why: Fact 1 and capital (Fact 4): growth replaces the most expensive etch module, using domestic carbon and iron.

title: Lay the capacitor down: MLCC-style 30-electrode stacks inside each cell
idea: Rearrange from tall-and-thin to flat-and-many: deposit 30 alternating TiN/Nb2O5 layers, pattern 180 nm cells with two offset staircase edge contacts so odd and even electrodes interleave like a ceramic MLCC; capacitance comes from layer count, not etch depth or litho.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) at 180 nm: 0.2 um2 x 30 layers x ~40 fF/um2 ~ 240 fF per cell, enough for 4-bit multilevel storage, EUV-free (fact 4); risk is film stress and staircase contact yield.

title: Hippocampal sleep consolidation: in-cell ferroelectric backup at power-fail
idea: The brain stores new memories quickly in the hippocampus and consolidates them into cortex during sleep. Coat each DRAM capacitor's inner electrode with 3-4 nm HZO and run it below the coercive field as a linear DRAM cap. On a power-fail interrupt, energy from a package hold-up capacitor drives all rows to write each cell's charge into polarization within ~10 ms, and the state is restored at power-up.
why: Data survive power loss while normal operation keeps DRAM speed and unlimited endurance. The ferroelectric switches only at power events, so ~10^5 lifetime cycles are enough.

title: Leakage decay as built-in recency weighting for analog KV caches
idea: Invert 'charge decay is a failure that refresh must undo' -> make decay part of the math. KV-cache and state-space values are stored as un-refreshed analog charge whose leakage time constant is programmed per bank by body bias, so stored magnitude decays exponentially with token age, implementing the recency weighting (decay gates, ALiBi-like bias) models already learn.
why: Eliminates refresh for the largest AI memory consumer (fact 3) and stores 4-6 analog bits per cell, multiplying effective capacity 4-6x for inference KV caches.

title: Atomically precise one-nanometer gold clusters as room-temperature Coulomb-blockade bits
idea: Derive the island from e2/2C >= 25 kT at 300 K: C <= 0.12 aF, a sub-1 nm island, which lithography cannot make but chemistry can (Au25(SR)18 clusters, ~1 eV charging gaps). Trap one cluster per cell between multiple tunnel junctions, store 0/1/2 electrons, and read with a single-electron-transistor electrometer, using the Coulomb staircase for 2 bits per cell.
why: Bits held as countable electrons need ~1 electron, not 31,000. Targets ~1e4x less stored charge, sub-aJ writes and multi-level density (facts 1, 10).

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings using 3D NAND tier stacks
idea: Fuse 1970s CCD memory with 3D NAND's stacked-gate vertical channel: 128 wordline tiers around a vertical poly-Si or IGZO channel are clocked in three phases to shift charge packets up and down, so bits live as packets in potential wells with no per-bit capacitor or lateral transistor. A sense amp at the string top reads packets as they arrive: serial within a string, massively parallel across millions of strings.
why: Fact 2: a 3D storage element with no capacitor and no lateral transistor, reusing NAND tooling; 5-10x bits per mm2 at block-sequential latency of a few hundred ns.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated plate stack inside each storage node
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitor construction at nanoscale: fill a wide shallow trench with 12 alternating metal/high-k layers, then use selective lateral recess on opposite sidewalls (as MLCC end terminations alternate) so odd plates tie to the storage node and even plates to the plate line.
why: Fact 1: capacitance scales with deposited layer count, not etch aspect ratio; 12 plates at 3 nm high-k reach ~6 fF at AR <10, deleting the 60-75:1 etch.

title: Coral and stalagmite growth: VLS nanowire forests grown as capacitor electrodes
idea: Grow the electrode instead of etching it: place Al, Sn or Cu catalyst dots (CMOS-friendlier than gold) by dewetting or e-beam litho, grow 1-2-um vertical Si or SnO2 nanowires by vapor-liquid-solid growth in a university LPCVD furnace, where 100:1 aspect ratios come for free, then ALD-coat the dielectric and top electrode.
why: Fact 1: AR >=100:1 electrodes with no 70:1 plasma etch or its EUV-defined mask, removing the hardest capacitor process; nanowire leaning, collapse and catalyst contamination are the risks.

title: Single cut-mask splits each pillar into differential twin half-capacitors
idea: Avionics users fear neutron upsets; one added cut mask slices each cylindrical bottom electrode into two half-shells, each on its own access path, storing complementary charges. Reading the pair differentially doubles signal per stored charge, removes reference cells and half-VDD bitline noise, and a strike on one half cannot flip the comparison alone.
why: 2x effective sense margin per electron allows ~0.7 V arrays (fact 10) or shorter pillars (fact 1); costs one cut mask and a second access device per pillar.

title: Hemoglobin cooperativity: antiferroelectric window multiplies effective capacitance
idea: Hemoglobin releases most of its oxygen inside a narrow pressure window by cooperative switching. Bias the cell plate of an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich capacitor so the 0 and 1 node voltages straddle its field-induced AFE-to-FE transition. The transition releases extra polarization charge, giving k_eff ~80-150 within the 1 V swing.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): reaches the k~70 target with no new elements, for 2-3x Cs at the same AR or half the AR. It does not store in ferroelectric hysteresis, so endurance stays near DRAM.

title: Corrugated cardboard: charge-density-wave domain pattern as switchable bit
idea: Stimulus 'corrugated cardboard' (a frozen periodic ripple) -> a thin 1T-TaS2 flake whose charge-density wave is driven between an insulating commensurate-like state and a hidden metallic domain state by a ps-ns current pulse; resistance changes ~10x and the hidden state persists. Substrate strain is engineered to keep it metastable at operating temperature.
why: Among the fastest known electronic phase switches (ps) at fJ energy (fact 10) with nondestructive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Leakage-balanced loadless node that holds its own bit
idea: Worsen: let leakage only ever drain the storage node toward zero. Flip: design a 4T loadless cell on a ~$50k shuttle where the access transistors' off-current deliberately trickles charge into the high node while cross-coupled pull-downs sink the low node, so leakage itself holds the bit.
why: Eliminates refresh (fact 3) with 4 transistors instead of 6T SRAM and no capacitor; cheap to prove within 24 months.

title: Hula hoop: persistent supercurrent loops at liquid-nitrogen temperature
idea: Stimulus 'hula hoop' (keeps circling once started) -> store a flux quantum in a YBCO nanoloop with a weak link, operated in a 77 K liquid-nitrogen rack memory pool rather than a helium cryostat; current circulates indefinitely and a nearby flux sensor reads its direction.
why: Zero-leakage, zero-refresh storage (fact 3) with aJ switching energy (fact 10), and avoids helium (Qatar supply offline) by using abundant LN2 for pooled memory.

title: Eliminate sputtered magnetic stacks: electroplated vertical racetracks in alumina pores
idea: Eliminate per-bit cells and argon-sputtered MTJ stacks: electroplate Co/Ni nanowires with composition modulated every 20 nm (built-in pinning notches) into 2-5 um anodic alumina pores, and shift magnetic domain walls past one read/write head at each pore base with current pulses; each pore holds ~100 bits.
why: 10-100x density per footprint without building tiers (fact 2), plating instead of PVD, refresh-free and nonvolatile; risks are domain-wall shift reliability and current density.

title: Nanopore-sequencer molecular tape with rewritable monomer charge
idea: Adapt Oxford Nanopore sequencing: a charged polymer shuttles back and forth through a solid-state nanopore; a write electrode oxidizes or reduces ferrocene side groups as they pass, and the pore current reads them back.
why: 10x at same cost: ~1 bit per nm of polymer coiled in a nanoreservoir; sequential like a racetrack but at molecular density, suited to warm-tier memory.

title: Threshold-switch selector stacked on capacitor for cross-point 3D DRAM
idea: Fuse the ovonic threshold switch selector from 3D XPoint with a MIM capacitor into a two-terminal 1S1C stack at each wordline/bitline crossing, built in 8-16 decks with no transistor. Half-select bias stays below the OTS threshold to isolate the node; a full-select pulse snaps the OTS on to charge or sense it.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 4F2 per deck with no front-end transistor; 8 decks ~5x density per wafer; requires OTS sub-threshold leakage below ~1 fA.

title: Spin-crossover molecular dielectric with room-temperature hysteresis
idea: Combine iron(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes, which switch between low-spin and high-spin states with ~10% volume and permittivity change and show 20-40 K wide hysteresis around room temperature, with a capacitor read: a local heating or field pulse flips the molecular layer, and capacitance reports the state. The bistable spin state holds without power.
why: Zero refresh in a ~5 nm molecular layer that could stack densely; switching speed and cycling endurance are the risks.

title: 3D XPoint selector film gating vertical sidewall capacitors
idea: Adapt Optane's threshold selector and vertical-RRAM geometry: a vertical bitline pillar crosses 48 word planes, and at each plane the sidewall carries a mixed-ionic-electronic selector film in series with a 4 nm MIM capacitor, making a transistor-free two-terminal 1S1C cell.
why: 10x at same cost: 48 planes share one hole litho, so even with ms retention bits per footprint rise ~15x; requires selector half-bias leakage below ~1 fA.

title: LiDAR SPAD avalanche gain reads attofarad storage nodes
idea: Adapt single-photon avalanche diodes: store ~300 electrons on a 50 aF node and read by dumping them into a linear-mode avalanche junction (gain ~100) beside the bitline, so the cell is a 4F2 vertical transistor plus junction with no capacitor.
why: 10x at same cost: deleting the capacitor allows 4F2 at a tighter SAQP pitch (F ~8 nm) and two stacked tiers, ~10x bits per area without the EUV-heavy capacitor module.
